steps.prompt: Which one makes you more curious?
steps.a: I went to the store and bought some milk and then I went back home.
steps.b: Bought milk. Came home. Door open.
steps.reveal: The second one uses only six words, but your brain fills in the rest. Who opened the door? That's the power of a six-word story.

cards.title: What is a six-word story?
cards.body: A whole story in exactly six words. It hints at what happened, and the reader's imagination does the rest.

cards.title: Every word has a job
cards.text: Found a puppy. Kept it secretly.
cards.note: "Found" starts the action. "Secretly" adds a problem: what happens when someone finds out?

cards.title: Spot the change
cards.prompt: Tap the two words that show what changed and what stayed the same.
cards.text: Old house. New family. Same creaky stairs.

cards.title: Tips for six-word stories
cards.body: Start in the middle of the action. Leave a question in the reader's mind. Cut little words like "the" and "a" when you can.

prompts: Which word in your six-word story are you proudest of? Why?
What question do you hope your reader asks after reading it?
